title: tri-sdk-compact-credential-profiles-and-stream-operator-harmony
author: Maya Chen
title_line: Tri-SDK: compact credential profiles + stream operator convergence
description: Motivation: multiple SDK teams have drifted in how credential lifecycles and stream operators are expressed. This causes ergonomic gaps for cross-language customers and duplicate runtime behavior. This PR introduces a small, explicit 'compact credential profile' model plus a unified stream operator surface across Python/TS/Go SDKs so common patterns (prefetch, lease windows, retry presets) are expressed consistently. Scope: changes touch auth orchestration and stream helpers in each SDK; no transport protocol changes. Key goals: (1) provide a tiny, well-documented credential profile that maps to server-side TTL/lease semantics; (2) expose a single stream operator abstraction that supports pause/resume, heartbeat, and backoff presets; (3) align default retry/backoff presets so cross-lang examples match; (4) bump SDK minors for compatibility. Backwards compatibility: existing credential factories still work (adapter added). Consumers can opt into new compact profiles via an explicit constructor. Migration notes included below. Implementation summary: - Python: add redwood.auth.CompactCredProfile, compact adapter layer, stream_ops.StreamOperator with heartbeat/backoff helpers, examples updated in examples/tri_sdk/ - TypeScript: add CompactCredProfile type and CredAdapter, export StreamOperator class with small fluent API; docs and typed examples added to docs/ - Go: introduce compact profile struct, CredAdapter interface shim, and streamoperator package with lightweight helpers; keep old constructors with deprecation notice. Testing: unit tests added for profile mapping, stream heartbeat, and combined integration tests exercising token swap and pause/resume. CI: flaky test fixed by adding a deterministic clock in stream operator tests. Rollout: bump Python to v1.16.0, TS to v1.28.1, Go to v1.8.3. Release notes and examples updated. Linear/ENG references are in the PR body.
commits: feat(stream): unified StreamOperator abstraction and heartbeat/backoff presets
test: add deterministic clock to stream operator tests to eliminate flakiness
refactor(ts): export CredAdapter types and update examples
refactor(go): cred adapter shim and streamoperator package
docs: add tri-sdk migration guide and API reference snippets
chore: bump SDK minors (py v1.16.0 / ts v1.28.1 / go v1.8.3)
reviews: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): This looks good overall; one concern about the default lease jitter — can we make that configurable per-profile?
Maya Chen (author): Good point — added jitter configuration to CompactCredProfile with a sensible default and documented it in the migration guide.
Priya Singh (reviewer): Please ensure the TS StreamOperator curries the same backoff presets as Python; I spot-checked the implementation and it matches but add a unit test to guarantee parity.
Maya Chen (author): Added unit test ts/tests/stream/stream_operator_presets.test.ts and updated README examples to show the equivalent call patterns.
Ethan Morales (reviewer): Integration looked stable; please add a short note in the release notes about how existing CredFactories map to CompactCredProfile to reduce support tickets.
Maya Chen (author): Added mapping notes and a short troubleshooting FAQ in docs/tri-sdk/compact-cred-profiles.md.
ci_history_notes: Initial run: unit/go had one flaky test (streamoperator timing) — reproduced locally and fixed by introducing deterministic clock in tests.
Re-run: all checks green; integration run exercised pause/resume and token swap flow against staging auth service.
discussion_highlights: Decision: keep new API additive; existing factories are wrapped by an adapter to ensure no immediate breaking changes.
Tradeoff: chosen a small surface for StreamOperator to avoid tying SDks to large lifecycle policies — we can iterate based on early adopter feedback.
Telemetry: added a minimal metric (sdk.stream.operator.heartbeats) to help diagnose missed heartbeats in the first weeks after release.
manual_tests: Smoke: launched sample tri-sdk chat example that rotates credentials every 45s while streaming long-running responses; validated no token errors.
Migration: ran compatibility shim against several internal services that still used legacy CredFactory; no regressions observed.
release_notes:
- Introduce CompactCredProfile across Python/TS/Go to express concise credential TTL/lease semantics.
- Add unified StreamOperator (pause/resume, heartbeat, backoff presets) for cross-language parity.
- Minor version bumps: Python v1.16.0, TypeScript v1.28.1, Go v1.8.3.
- Migration: existing CredFactories are automatically adapted; see docs/tri-sdk/compact-cred-profiles.md for mapping and examples.
merge_outcome: merged into main after approvals from all reviewers; changelog updated and publish jobs triggered for SDK registry
notes_to_release_manager: Tag and publish SDK artifacts after CI verification. Watch heartbeats metric for first 48 hours post-release; roll back quickly if increased token swap failures observed.
post_merge_actions: Create a short internal onboarding doc for solutions engineers with migration examples (assigned: Maya).
Monitor sdk.stream.operator.heartbeats and sdk.auth.token.swap_failures for 7 days.
Coordinate minor SDK releases in each language with Developer Experience team.
